approve(address,uint256).details: Approve the address _spender to spend the specified amount of tokens on behalf of msg.sender. Beware that changing an allowance with this method brings the risk that someone may use both the old and the new allowance by unfortunate transaction ordering. One possible solution to mitigate this race condition is to first reduce the spender's allowance to 0 and set the desired value afterwards: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/20#issuecomment-263524729

params._spender: The address that will be allowed to spend the tokens.
params._value: The amount of tokens to be spent.

changeTransferProvider(address).details: Sets a new transfers control provider contract address.

params._newProvider: The address of the new transfers control contract.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5,05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the value {ERC20} uses, unless this function is overridden; NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

decreaseSupply(address,uint256).details: Destroys `_value` tokens from `_wallet`, deducting from the caller's allowance. The caller must have allowance for ``_wallet``'s tokens of at least `_value`.

params._value: The number of tokens to destroy.

returns.success: A boolean that indicates if the operation was successful.

freeze(address).details: Freezes address balance from being transferred.

getFeeFor(uint256).details: Calculates the fee for a given value

params._value: The amount to get the fee for.

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

increaseSupply(address,uint256).details: Increases the total supply by minting the specified number of tokens to the specified wallet address

params._value: The number of tokens to add.

returns.success: A boolean that indicates if the operation was successful.

initialize(address,address,uint8,uint8,a.details: Initializes the contract by the proxy

params._assetProtectionRole: The role id that is allowed to freeze/unfreeze addresses and seize their tokens.
params._initTransferProvider: The address of the transfers control contract.
params._owner: The owner of the contract (usually an instance of vnxManager).
params._rbac: The address of the role-based access control contract.
params._supplyControllerRole: The role id that is allowed to burn/mint tokens to control supply.
params._symbol: The short name of the token.

isAdmin().details: Returns true if the caller is the admin role

isFrozen(address).details: Checks whether the address is currently frozen.

returns._0: A bool representing whether the given address is frozen.

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pause().details: Pauses all transfer operations on token

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

reclaimTokensFromFrozenAddress(address).details: Reclaim the DGRs from a specific frozen user address and send them to the wallet of the sender (asset protection and supply control address).

params._addr: The frozen address to reclaim the tokens from.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions anymore. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby removing any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setAssetProtectionRole(uint8).details: Sets a new asset protection role id.

params._newAssetProtectionRole: The new role id that is allowed to freeze/unfreeze addresses and seize their tokens.

params._newFeeRate: The new fee rate to be applied to the calculation of transfer fees for transfers.

setFeeRecipient(address).details: Sets a new fee recipient address.

params._newFeeRecipient: The address to accumulate transfer fees for transfers.

setSupplyControllerRole(uint8).details: Sets a new supply controller role id.

params._newSupplyControllerRole: The new role id that is allowed to burn/mint tokens to control supply.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transfer(address,uint256).details: Transfer the tokens to a specified address from msg.sender

transferAnyERC20Token(address,address,ui.details: The admin can transfer out any ERC20 tokens accidentally sent to this contract address

params._amount: The amount of tokens to be transferred.
params._to: The address to transfer the tokens to.
params._token: the address of the ERC20 token that needs to be transferred.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: Transfer the tokens from one address to another

params._from: address The address that you want to send the tokens from
params._to: address The address that you want to transfer to
params._value: uint256 the amount of tokens to be transferred

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

unpause().details: Unpauses all transfer operations on token
